intent: Grok critique E5: the threat model was unstated. Write it down explicitly and honestly — name the primary scenario, state the trust assumption, and name (not hide) what is out of current scope. This is a DOCS-only artifact: no code, no gate behavior, no policy change.
riskRationale: Documentation only. No code or gate/policy change, so no behavior to verify beyond 'tests still green'. The risk is over-claiming scope in prose; guarded by naming out-of-scope adversaries explicitly as known limits / future work rather than implying coverage.

constraints.detail: Primary adversary/scenario stated plainly: ACCIDENTAL purpose-bound leakage in a benign agent — it fetched data for task A and then helpfully included it in unrelated output B. No malice assumed.

Explicitly out of current scope and named: (1) a prompt-injection adversary actively trying to exfiltrate, (2) a malicious tool that lies about declared purpose, (3) semantic/paraphrased leaks where the agent restates the secret in different words. Written as known limits / future work.
Trust assumption stated: the gate sees the tool results + the drafted outbound and trusts the declared purpose labels. It does not verify a declared purpose is honest and does not infer intent.
Prose contains no '->' arrows; voice matches the human-first site standard. Short, grounded section in README.md plus full docs/threat-model.md.
bun test = 16 pass / 0 fail (83 expect() calls). Docs-only change touched no code; suite unchanged.
Only README.md (new Threat model section), docs/threat-model.md (new), and this receipt changed. src/ and test/ untouched; no gate or policy edit.

observations.detail: docs/threat-model.md is the canonical statement; README.md carries a short pointer-and-summary version for the first read.
Out-of-scope adversaries are named in the open, and the trust-in-labels assumption is stated as a limit, not spun as a feature.

actions.detail: Added docs/threat-model.md and a Threat model section to README.md
actions.result: primary scenario + trust assumption + named out-of-scope items

assertions.detail: the claim is bounded to accidental leakage in a benign agent with trusted labels
no behavior change; gate output and tests unchanged

mechanisms: A stated threat model lets a reader judge fit in seconds and stops the gate from being mistaken for an anti-exfiltration or anti-injection control.
The named out-of-scope items (injection, malicious tool, paraphrase) are the explicit backlog for later iterations.
